sources.citation: Yu, C. & Smith, L. B. (2007). Rapid word learning under uncertainty via cross-situational statistics. Psychological Science 18(5).
sources.use: Multiple ambiguous word-referent exposures can be informative through cross-situational co-occurrence; motivates the non-oracular repeated-occurrence fixture.

sources.citation: Fazly, A., Alishahi, A. & Stevenson, S. (2010). A probabilistic computational model of cross-situational word learning. Cognitive Science 34(6).
sources.use: Probabilistic alignment normalized against co-occurring words motivates explicit within-episode competition instead of independent token fits.

sources.citation: Dempster, A. P., Laird, N. M. & Rubin, D. B. (1977). Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm. JRSS B 39(1).
sources.use: Motivates repeated latent-assignment and parameter-update iterations; v4 does not claim its custom objective is a likelihood-equivalent EM implementation.

sources.citation: Efron, B. (1987). Better bootstrap confidence intervals. JASA 82(397).
sources.use: Supports predeclared bootstrap inference while v4 explicitly branches away from undefined studentization under zero variance.
Documents that degenerate bootstrap distributions can yield invalid intervals, motivating an explicit labelled degenerate-data branch rather than silent NaNs or an empty quantile call.

scope_note: Sources constrain method design only. No source was used to tune a language outcome, and no restricted or AEA material was accessed.
